Abstract: Herein, we report regiodiverg ent nucleophilic attack of Grignard reagents to 2-alkynyl aziridines.
Under the catalysis of a Cu(I)-diphosphine complex, benzylic Grignard reagents add to the carbon-carbon
triple bond of the aziridines to deliver α-allenylamines in moderate to excellent yields; the direct addition of
the Grignard reagents to the aziridines in the absence of catalyst provided homopropar gylic amine derivatives.
Both reactions could proceed in highly enantiospecific ways. Further synthetic manipulations of these products
enable rapid access to diverse useful heterocyclic molecular scaff olds.
Keywords: aziridines; ring opening; Grignard reagents; alkynes; allenes
Intr oduction
Owing to the presence of both the strained aziridine ring
and the alkyne bond, 2-alkynl aziridines represent a
particular class of synthetic building blocks with multi-
ple reactive sites for accessing diverse useful nitrogen-
containing molecules while attracting much research
intention.
[1]
Whilst the nucleophilic ring opening reac-
tions of 2-alkyl or aryl aziridines usually proceed via an
S
N
2-type mechanism,
[2]
the reaction with 2-alkynyl
aziridines may proceed via S
N
2-type and/or S
N
2’-type
mechanisms to provide alkynyl products and/or allenic
products. Oxygen nucleophiles,
[3]
especially phenols,
have been reported to attack the aziridine ring to
predominantly provide alkynyl products with elegant
applications to the syntheses of complex bioactive
molecules such as ustiloxin
[4]
and phomopsin B.
[5]
Relevant reaction systems with other nucleophiles such
as nitrogen- and sulphur -nucleophiles have also been
developed with varied degrees of success
(Scheme 1a).
[3c,6]
On the other hand, highly regioselective and
enantiospecific nucleophilic attacks at the carbon-carbon
triple bond in 2-alkynyl aziridines (mostly bearing a
terminal alkyne) to generate allenic products have been
realized with traditional reactive org anometallic reagents
such as org anolithium and org anomaganesium under the
mediation of stoichiometric amounts of Cu(I) salts

In contrast, relevant catalytic reaction

[7b]
Notably , sporadic examples of Cu(I)-
catalyzed borylative

and silylative
[10]

2-alkynyl aziridines to allenic products have also been
recently reported.
[1 1]
W e report herein regiodiverg ent
reactions of 2-alkynyl aziridines with Grignard reagents.
W ith a catalytic amount of a Cu(I) salt, the reaction
provided β-allenylamine products with good to excellent
yields, whereas in the absence of the Cu(I) salt,
homopropar gylic amine products were obtained instead
(Scheme 1c).
Results and Discussion
W e initiated the study by screening the reaction
conditions for the model reaction between aziridine 1 a
and the Grignard reagent 2 a (T able 1). After a prelimi-

presence of a phosphine ligand directed the reaction to
the formation of the allenic product 3 aa with high
selectivity and DPPF turned out to be the optimum
ligand (T able 1, entry 5). Notably , previous relevant
studies have been mainly restricted to aziridines bearing
a terminal alkyne moiety ,
[7–8]
and the current study first
incorporates aziridines bearing an aryl alkyne into such
a transformation. Unfortunately , the use of several chiral
phosphine and BOX ligands hardly provided any chiral
induction in both the product and the recovered aziridine
(see T able S1 in the SI for details). An obvious solvent
ef fect on the reaction was also observed: the use of
toluene, MTBE and Et

the ligand or the catalyst combination or increasing the

Subsequently , we examined the reaction scope with
regard to the formation of the allenic products 3
(T able 2). In general, the reaction tolerated well a range
of aziridines bearing (hetero)aryl-, silyl- and alkyl-
substituted and terminal alkyne moieties to provide the
desired products in high yields. In some cases, in
addition to the allenic products, the S
N
2-type ring-
opening products were also obtained in considerable
amounts (4 fa, 4 ga and 4 ha). The gram-scale prepara-
tion of the product 4 aa in a comparable yield
demonstrates the practicality of this reaction. Notably ,
2,2-disubstituted proparg ylic aziridine disfavoured the
S
N
2-type ring opening while preferring the formation of
the tetrasubstituted allenic product (3 ha vs 3 ia). It’ s
worth noting that the N-Boc counterpart of aziridine 1a
was not tolerated in this reaction in that only the
aziridine (1n) was recovered (55%) after a prolonged
reaction time of 48 h, together with the formation of
unidentified complex mixture. The aziridine 1o bearing
two methyl groups at the 3-position also gave a poor
yield of the desired product together with the recovery
of starting material and the formation of unidentified
mixtures. As to the scope of Grignard reagents in the
reaction with aziridine 1 a, benzylic Grignard reagents
bearing diff erent substituents on the benzene ring were
suitable for the reaction to provide the allenic products
in generally high yields. Surprisingly , the reaction with
4’-cholorobenzylmagnesium bromide gave 18% of
homopropar gylic amine product 4 af together with 60%
of 3 af. For the primary alkyl Grignard reagents, the
regioselectivity for the ring opening is poor in that the
two types of products were obtained in comparable
yields (3 ag and 4 ag). In the case of isopropylmagne-
sium bromide, only the homopropar gylic amine product
4 ah was obtained in 95% yield. The use of correspond-
ing phenyl or isopropenyl Grignard reagents all
furnished the alkynyl products as the major products
(4ai and 4aj). Notably , alkyl Grignard reagents have
been shown to under go S
N
2’-type reaction with prop-
ar gylic ammonium salts with excellent
regioselectivity .
[12]
The use of ethynylmagnesium
bromide (2k) in this reaction with the aziridine 1 a
hardly produced any desired product while 57% of the
aziridine was recovered together with unidentifiable
complex mixture. The use of either 2-meth-
ylallylmagnesium chloride (2l) or the organolithium
reagent n-BuLi produced a complex reaction mixture.
[13]
The structure of the product 3 ca was determined by
single crystal x-ray crystallographic analysis (CCDC
2391017).
[14]
Next, the scope of the S
N
2-type ring opening reaction
of 2-alkynyl aziridines was investigated (T able 3). For
aziridines bearing aryl alkyne moieties, the reaction
proceeded smoothly to provide the desired homopropar-
gylic amine products in good to excellent yields (4 aa–
4 ga). The reaction could also be performed on gram-
scale as demonstrated in the case of 4 aa. While good
yields could be obtained with aziridines bearing silyl
alkynes, the reaction with those bearing alkyl-substi-
tuted alkynes provided allenic products (3 ja and 3 ka)
as major products. The aziridine 1 l bearing a terminal
alkyne was also not tolerated in this reaction to provide
the allenic product (3 la) in a low yield together with
unidentifiable complex mixture. The use of substituted
benzylic Grignard reagents generally provided moderate
yields in this reaction while the corresponding allenic
products and/or other unidentified side products were
formed concomitantly (4 ab–4 af). In addition, alkyl and
aryl Grignard reagents provided low yields of the
desired products (4 ag–4 ai) together with unidentifiable
complex mixture. It’s worth noting that in the presence
of the Cu(I)-dppf complex, the homopropar gylic amine
products 4 ah and 4 ai were obtained in high yields
(T able 2). V inyl (2j) and ethynyl (2k) Grignard reagents
were not tolerated in this reaction to give complex

a result is reminiscent of early findings that allylic
Grignard reagents tend to undergo 1,2-addition to α,β-
unsaturated carbonyl compounds, which could be
accommodated by a six-membered-ring transition
state.
[15]
Under the standard reaction conditions, the regiodi-
vergent reactions between enantioenriched aziridine (S)-
1 a and the Grignard reagent 2 a proceeded smoothly to
provide the desired products with high enantiospecific-
ity (Scheme 2a). The absolute configurations of the two
products were unambiguously confirmed by single
crystal x-ray crystallographic analysis,
[14]
which supports
that the allenic product (R)-3 aa (CCDC 2391015) might
be formed via an anti-S
N
2’-type mechanism
[7b]
and the
homopropar gylic amine product (R)-4 aa (CCDC
2391016) might be formed via an S
N
2-type mechanism.
In previous relevant studies on copper-c atalyzed reac-
tions between Grignard reagents and proparg ylic elec-
trophiles involving C � N bond cleavage,
[12]
the gener-
ation of Gilman-type org anocuprates have been
proposed and their tendency to attack carbon-carbon
triple bond might be attributed to the “softer” nature of
them according to hard and soft acid and base
concept.
[16]
The α-allenylamine
[17]
product 3 aa could
under go an acid-catalyzed intramolecular hydroamina-
tion to produce compound 5, the structure of which was
confirmed by single crystal x-ray crystallographic
analysis (CCDC 2391014).
[14]
Notably , when a sample
of enantioenriched (R)-3aa (94% ee) was subjected to
the otherwise same conditions, the product (S)-5 was
obtained in 59% yield and 85% ee. Detosylation of 5
with SmI
2
furnished the dihydropyrrole 6 in a moderate
yield (Scheme 2b). Synthetically useful (Z)- and (E)-
homoallylic amines 7 could be prepared in excellent
yields from the homopropar gylic amine product 4 aa.
[18]
Conclusion
In summary , the regiodiver gent ring opening reactions
of 2-alkynyl aziridines with Grignard reagents has been
investigated. Depending mainly on the use of a Cu(I)
catalyst or the Grignard reagents, the ring opening
reaction might proceed via either an anti-S
N
2’-type
pathway to provide α-allenylamine products or an S
N
2-
type mechanism to furnish homopropar gylic amine
products. The reaction is scalable and occurs in a highly
enantiospecific fashion with enantioenriched 2-alkynyl
aziridines.

Abstract: Herein, we report regiodivergent nucleophilic attack of Grignard reagents to 2-alkynyl aziridines.
Under the catalysis of a Cu(I)-diphosphine complex, benzylic Grignard reagents add to the carbon-carbon
triple bond of the aziridines to deliver α-allenylamines in moderate to excellent yields; the direct addition of
the Grignard reagents to the aziridines in the absence of catalyst provided homopropargylic amine derivatives.
Both reactions could proceed in highly enantiospecific ways. Further synthetic manipulations of these products
enable rapid access to diverse useful heterocyclic molecular scaffolds.
Keywords: aziridines; ring opening; Grignard reagents; alkynes; allenes
Introduction

Owing to the presence of both the strained aziridine ring
and the alkyne bond, 2-alkynl aziridines represent a
particular class of synthetic building blocks with multi-
ple reactive sites for accessing diverse useful nitrogen-
containing molecules while attracting much research
intention.<sup>[1]</sup> Whilst the nucleophilic ring opening reac-
tions of 2-alkyl or aryl aziridines usually proceed via an
\mathrm { S } _ { \mathrm { N } } 2 \mathrm { - } \mathrm { t y p e }
mechanism,<sup>[2]</sup> the reaction with 2-alkynyl
aziridines may proceed via
\mathrm { S } _ { \mathrm { N } } 2 { \ - } \mathrm { - } \mathrm { t y p e }
and/or
\mathrm { S _ { N } } 2 ^ { \prime } { \mathrm { - t y p e } }
mechanisms to provide alkynyl products and/or allenic
products. Oxygen nucleophiles,<sup>[3]</sup> especially phenols,
have been reported to attack the aziridine ring to
predominantly provide alkynyl products with elegant
applications to the syntheses of complex bioactive
molecules such as ustiloxin<sup>[4]</sup> and phomopsin B.<sup>[5]</sup>
Relevant reaction systems with other nucleophiles such
as nitrogen- and sulphur-nucleophiles have also been
developed with varied degrees of success
(Scheme 1a).<sup>[3c,6]</sup>

On the other hand, highly regioselective and
enantiospecific nucleophilic attacks at the carbon-carbon
triple bond in 2-alkynyl aziridines (mostly bearing a
terminal alkyne) to generate allenic products have been
realized with traditional reactive organometallic reagents
a) Nucleophilic ring opening of 2-alkynl aziridines to propargylic products (refs. 3-6):
b) Cu(l)-mediated ring opening of 2-alkynl aziridines to allenic products (refs. 7-8):
c) Regiodivergent reactions of 2-alkynl aziridines with RMgBr (this work)

(Scheme 1b), which typically require cryogenic

Conclusion

In summary, the regiodivergent ring opening reactions
of 2-alkynyl aziridines with Grignard reagents has been
investigated. Depending mainly on the use of a Cu(I)
catalyst or the Grignard reagents, the ring opening
reaction might proceed via either an
a n t i - S _ { \mathrm { { N } } } \bar { 2 } ^ { \prime }
-type
pathway to provide α-allenylamine products or an
\mathrm { S } _ { \mathrm { N } } 2 \cdot
type mechanism to furnish homopropargylic amine
products. The reaction is scalable and occurs in a highly
enantiospecific fashion with enantioenriched 2-alkynyl
aziridines.
